jobs.title: Director of Industrialisation
jobs.description:
Help Build Europe's Hypersonic Capability
 
At Hypersonica, we’re redefining what’s possible in European defence technology. We exist to deliver speed, resilience, and technological independence at a pace that sets a new standard. We are a small, elite team working on problems that matter, and solving them fast.
 
By joining Hypersonica, you’re not stepping into a predefined role. You’re joining a talent dense environment where every individual shapes the direction of the company. Our philosophy is to hire a small number of exceptional people with broad, deep technical capability, strong judgement, and the ability to operate autonomously.
 
We hire for talent, not rigid boxes. This role represents a business need, but the way it evolves will be shaped by the individual. If you’ve achieved what others said was impossible, or you bring a unique combination of skills that doesn’t fit a traditional mould, we want to hear from you. The work you do here directly contributes to Europe’s technological independence.

Getting complex hardware through development and into flight is one challenge. Building the industrial capability to deliver it repeatedly, at the required quality and rate, is another. We’re looking for a Director of Industrialisation to lead that work in Germany.

You’ll take a greenfield manufacturing site from an empty floor to sustained series production. You’ll shape the facility, decide what we build in-house, bring in the equipment and people, and lead the ramp until the operation can deliver reliably. Your job starts while the product is still taking shape, when the right manufacturing decision can save months of work later.

We’re looking for someone who’s done this before and wants to build again. You’ll work directly with the founders and with Engineering, Programmes, Quality, Supply Chain and Operations. You’ll be close enough to the floor to see where the plan is breaking down, and senior enough to make the decisions that fix it.


What you’ll do

  • Own the industrialisation plan. Translate programme demand into a plan for capacity, capital investment, people and suppliers. Set milestones from facility readiness through pilot builds and production ramp, and make the trade-offs visible when timelines or assumptions change.

  • Build and commission the operation. Define what the site needs to support, shape the layout and material flow, and lead equipment selection, installation and commissioning. Plan how the operation will expand as demand grows.

  • Bring manufacturing into product decisions early. Work with Engineering to make the hardware practical to build, inspect and test. Bring evidence from the floor into design reviews, and agree how changes will be introduced as the design matures.

  • Decide what to make and what to buy. Work with Supply Chain to establish which capabilities we need to own, where specialist suppliers make sense, and how we qualify and scale those suppliers alongside our own production.

  • Take pilot builds into repeatable production. Use early builds to expose what will limit output. Resolve bottlenecks, improve yield and build consistency, and demonstrate that the operation can sustain its target rate across successive builds.

  • Build the team and the way it works. Hire the people who will establish the operation. Give them clear ownership, develop leaders on the floor, and put in place the training and routines that let the team solve problems as production grows.

  • Own manufacturing readiness. Define the evidence needed before increasing the rate, from process capability and trained operators to supplier readiness, inspection and traceability. Work with Quality and Safety to build those requirements into everyday work.

  • Make the hard calls. Decide where automation earns its place, where a simpler process gets us there sooner, and where to commit capital before all the answers are in. Give leadership a clear view of what’s on track, what’s at risk and what decision is needed.


    • Who you are

  • You’ve personally led a greenfield site or a major production operation built from scratch, through commissioning and into sustained series or volume production. You can tell us what existed on day one, what you owned and what the operation was delivering once it ramped.

  • You’ve industrialised complex hardware while the design was still evolving. You know how to keep engineering and manufacturing moving together when a design change affects tooling, suppliers, inspection or the delivery plan.

  • You’ve made consequential capital, capacity and staffing decisions. You can explain what you committed to early, what you deliberately kept flexible and how those choices played out.

  • You’ve lived through a difficult ramp. You can talk us through a target you missed, how you found the real constraint, what you changed and what happened to output, yield, cost or delivery as a result.

  • You’ve built and led teams across disciplines. You can earn the trust of operators, technicians and engineers, challenge a design decision with evidence, and explain a manufacturing trade-off to the founders in plain language.

  • You know how to build at pace in a demanding hardware environment. You put the controls that matter in place early, and keep decisions close to the people doing the work.

  • You’re motivated by the opportunity to build industrial capability for European defence, and you want to be on site with the team doing it.


    • Where you might have done it
    You might have launched a new factory in automotive, built a production operation at a hardware startup, or taken an aerospace or advanced manufacturing product from low-rate builds to series production.
     
    You could have done it inside a larger company if you had the mandate to build the operation and were personally accountable for the ramp.The common thread is the build itself. We want to hear about the operation you created, how quickly you brought it online, the rate it sustained and the decisions you made when the original plan met reality.

    What we offer

  • Genuine ownership of the industrialisation of one of Europe’s most ambitious defence engineering programmes, from an empty site to sustained series production.

  • The chance to join early enough that your decisions will shape the factory, the team and how Hypersonica manufactures for years to come.

  • Direct access to the founders and the factory floor, with short decision paths and the authority to act when you see a better way to build.

  • Daily collaboration with exceptional people across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Test and Programmes. You’ll have a seat at the table while the product is still taking shape.

  • The freedom to challenge convention and build from first principles, from what we make in-house to where automation earns its place.

  • The resources and ambition to build a production operation at a pace that would be hard to match in a traditional aerospace organisation.

  • The chance to see your decisions through, from the first factory layout on a whiteboard to hardware coming off a line that delivers reliably, shift after shift.

    • At Hypersonica, every hire raises the bar. We are deliberately small, intensely capable, and deeply mission-driven. If this role feels like a strong fit, or if you believe you bring something exceptional that goes beyond the description, we encourage you to apply.
     
    Hypersonica is an equal-opportunity employer and assesses candidates solely on merit, capability, and potential.
     
    You can apply directly to this role or reach out to Nathan Sweeney, Head of Talent. We review every application and aim to respond to all candidates within two weeks, whether the answer is yes or no.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Product Structure & Systems (PLM/MES)
jobs.description:
ANYbotics is a fast-growing tech company dedicated to shaping the future of mobile robotics across multiple industries. Join our highly talented and motivated team of more than 200 people and work on cutting-edge robot technology.

The Opportunity

As the Senior Manager of Product Structure, PLM & MES, you are the architect of the digital backbone that connects our robotic innovations to real-world production. In this high-impact leadership role, you will strategically own the implementation and evolution of our Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Manufacturing Execution (MES) systems and processes to scale with a rapidly growing product and manufacturing organization ("Digital Thread").
You will govern the product architecture for our complex mechatronic systems, ensuring that our Engineering BOM (EBOM), Manufacturing BOM (MBOM), and Service BOM (SBOM) are perfectly synchronized. 
This is not just a systems role — it’s a business transformation mandate. You will define and execute the PLM and MES roadmap in collaboration with executive stakeholders, ensuring alignment between engineering, operations, product, and after-sales service functions. You’ll help us build an integrated, enterprise-grade ecosystem that accelerates product development, enables traceability, and scales product data excellence.

 
 

The Market & Our Technology

ANYbotics transforms industrial plants in the energy, process, and utility sector by introducing robotics to a wide range of novel applications that so far were beyond reach. Our customers are large asset operators and industrial service providers pioneering the use of robotics technology for inspection and maintenance. Our mobile robot ANYmal uses legs for extreme mobility in complex environments, camera- and LIDAR-based sensing for full autonomy and obstacle avoidance, and AI for high-quality and consistent inspection results. We develop numerous customized hardware systems, including the entire robotic platform, actuators, sensors, inspection payloads, charging systems, and all related ANYbotics mechanical hardware.


Your Impact
  • Product Structure & Configuration Governance
  • BOM Mastery: Define and govern multi-level BOM structures for complex robotic systems, ensuring alignment across Engineering, Manufacturing, and Service.
  • Modular Architecture: Support platform-based development by managing product configurations, variants, and component reuse strategies.
  • Data Standards: Enforce rigorous part-numbering schemes, revision control, and BOM rules to maintain 100% data integrity.
  • PLM System Ownership & Digital Thread
  • Platform Management: Own the strategic roadmap, implementation and functional administration of the PLM environment (e.g., Windchill, Teamcenter, CIM Database).
  • System Integration: Manage the technical "Digital Thread" between CAD → PLM → ERP → MES, ensuring real-time synchronization of product and manufacturing data.
  • Release Management: Oversee the lifecycle states, access controls, and workflows for all product releases and configuration baselines.
  • MES & Manufacturing Data Integration
  • Production Execution: Ensure the flawless transfer of product structures from PLM to the MES for production execution.
  • Process Definition: Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering to define production routings, assembly sequences, and digital work instructions in the MES.
  • Traceability: Maintain "As-Built" traceability, ensuring consistency between MES production data and ERP production orders.

  • Define the macOS and Jamf automation architecture, engineering standards and roadmap for a global Apple device service. 

  • Engineer automated packaging, deployment, update and rollback pipelines for macOS applications. 

  • Evaluate Jamf, Apple and related ecosystem capabilities, APIs and emerging technologies to simplify or extend the service. 

  • Troubleshoot complex failures across macOS, Jamf, identity, networking, security and application-delivery services. 

  • Convert recurring Mac incidents and support escalations into automated detection, remediation or prevention. 

  • Document designs, code, operating procedures and support models, and enable support teams to use them effectively. 

    •

  • 4+ years of experience engineering and automating macOS services in a modern enterprise environment.

  • Strong knowledge of macOS management, Apple Business Manager, Automated Device Enrollment, declarative device management and Apple security controls. 

  • Ability to build production-quality automation using shell scripting, Python, REST APIs and structured data formats, supported by Git, CI/CD, testing, secrets management, Jamf webhooks and code review. 

  • Experience automating macOS application packaging, deployment, patching and vulnerability remediation; a bachelor’s degree in IT or Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience. 

    •

  • Experience with identity integrations, Platform SSO, certificate services, zero-touch deployment and device trust. 

  • Knowledge of Installomator, swiftDialog, Nudge, or similar community and enterprise macOS automation tooling. 

  • Experience integrating Jamf with ServiceNow, asset-management, security, observability or data platforms. 

  • Cloud services, serverless functions, SQL or reporting technologies used to host integrations and analyse endpoint data. 

  • Familiarity with Microsoft Intune, Linux or mobile device management in a broader endpoint environment.

Redefine the future of live entertainment tech
 
Welcome to vivenu, the global leader in event ticketing tech and one of the world’s fastest-growing live entertainment tech firms. As a Data Engineering Lead, Agentic Infrastructure, you will be the foundational technical leader of our data organization, guiding a dedicated pod of engineers in the future. You will act as the technical authority and central hub for all data initiatives across the company, ensuring a cohesive, secure, and scalable data strategy.

Ensure that every data initiative goes through your team and aligns with our overarching architecture and scalability standards.
  • Lead & mentor: Provide technical leadership, architectural guidance, and hands-on mentorship to a high-impact team of engineers.
  • Drive company-wide AI adoption: Build the robust, reliable data pipelines and infrastructure required to power our internal AI initiatives, enabling intelligent tooling and automation.
  • Scale for the future: Establish a future-proof technical foundation that initially optimizes internal operations, with a clear roadmap to expand into core product features.
  • Establish operational excellence: Implement data governance, data lineage, observability, and strict quality controls to ensure the data platform is reliable and trusted.

    • What you will need to succeed in this role:
  • 8+ years of hands-on experience in Data Engineering, building modern data stacks, central data warehouses, and high-throughput data pipelines.
  • A track record of technically leading and elevating small teams while remaining deeply hands-on.
  • Proven ability to design company-wide data architectures and act as the principal technical decision-maker for complex data systems.
  • Strong understanding of how to structure, model, and pipeline data specifically to support AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics adoption.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to partner with internal stakeholders to centralize and streamline all business data requests.
  • Familiarity or hands-on experience with Agentic AI technologies, specifically building infrastructure where autonomous agents and AI models can learn, access data, and execute tasks.

    Live Entertainment Tech
    Play a mission-critical role for global brands, redefining fan experiences from festivals to major sports events. Here, you’re part of the business of fun — powered by cutting-edge technology that brings moments to life for millions.
     
    Sustainable Growth
    We scale sustainably on a profitable, VC-backed foundation with true product-market fit. This means continuous investment in our people, products, and long-term vision.
     
    Top-tier Team
    Collaborate with over 170 dedicated professionals, including leaders from Google, Slack, and Salesforce. Together, we’re shaping the future of live entertainment technology, one decision at a time.
     
    Global DNA
    We’re a diverse, merit-driven team spread across six global offices. Talent and impact are what matter here — not hierarchy or background.
     
    Fast Growing, in All Aspects
    Sifted consistently ranks us among the fastest-growing scale-ups in Europe. We’re driven by daily learning, shared wins, and collective growth.
     
    Next-Gen Leaders & Insights
    Work alongside some of tech’s brightest minds — from Forbes 30 Under 30 founders to Executive of the Year award winners. At vivenu, you’ll help set the standard for the ticketing industry’s future.
     
    vivenu Inclusion Statement
    At vivenu, we believe our people define our success – and that we win with bold, diverse minds. The strongest teams are built on different perspectives, experiences, and voices. We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels empowered to contribute, grow, and thrive to shape the future of live entertainment globally.

jobs.description:
Über uns:

HyPlus ist Dein Wegbegleiter im digitalen Wandel. Gemeinsam mit unseren Kund:innen entwickeln wir strukturiert, partnerschaftlich und mit klarem Fokus auf nachhaltigen Mehrwert, deren digitale DNA. Wir begleiten Unternehmen von der Anforderungsanalyse über Architektur, Softwareentwicklung und Implementierung bis hin zum Betrieb. Mit rund 800 Kolleg:innen in Deutschland, Polen, Litauen, Rumänien und Indien verbinden wir technologische Exzellenz mit Branchenkompetenz in Automotive, Handel, Banken & Versicherungen sowie dem öffentlichen Sektor.

Bei uns ist KI kein Innovationstheater. Wir betreiben einen eigenen GPU-Server, hosten Modelle selbst, betreiben einen eigenen AI Gateway und bauen für Kunden – insb. aus der Versicherungswirtschaft - Prozesse, die täglich echte Fälle entscheiden. Unser Center of Excellence AI ist die Stelle, an der neue Technologien zuerst ankommen, bewertet und dann in Projekte und in eine Guidance für unsere Mitarbeitenden übersetzt werden.

Wir suchen dafür jemanden, der/die wirklich tief drin ist: eine Person, die neue Modelle, Frameworks und Werkzeuge früh entdeckt, sie selbst ausprobiert und danach begründen kann, was davon in einem regulierten Unternehmensumfeld trägt und was nicht. Ungefähr 70 % der Zeit arbeitest du direkt in Kundenprojekten, rund 30 % gehören dem Center of Excellence (CoE) und damit der Frage, wo wir in achtzehn Monaten stehen.

Deine Aufgaben in Kundenprojekten:

  • Agentische Prozessautomatisierung: Du entwirfst und entwickelst Agenten und Workflows entlang realer Fachprozesse, beispielsweise für Schadenmeldungen, Dokumentenprüfungen oder Kunden-Onboarding, und entscheidest, wann KI oder klassische Logik sinnvoll ist

  • LLM- und Bild-KI-Module: Du integrierst Text-, Dokumenten- und Bildverarbeitung als API-basierte Module in produktive Anwendungen und sorgst für eine zuverlässige Datenanreicherung

  • Qualität messbar machen: Du entwickelst Testdatensätze, definierst Qualitätsmetriken und etablierst Regressionstests, um die Leistung von Modellen und Prompts messbar und zuverlässig zu machen

  • Architektur und Integration: Du integrierst KI-Komponenten in bestehende IT-Landschaften und triffst nachvollziehbare Architekturentscheidungen

  • Betrieb, Sicherheit und Compliance: Du verantwortest das Hosting von KI-Modellen auf eigener GPU-Infrastruktur sowie den AI Gateway und berücksichtigst Datenschutz, Sicherheit und EU AI Act

  • Inferenz-Betrieb und AI-DevOps: Du betreibst und optimierst offene KI-Modelle mit Technologien wie Ollama, vLLM, SGLang und TGI sowie Docker und Kubernetes und verantwortest automatisierte Deployments, Monitoring und Kostenkontrolle

  • Sparring im Presales: Du begleitest Kundentermine und Workshops, berätst Fachbereiche und bewertest technische Möglichkeiten, Kosten und Risiken

Deine Aufgaben im Center of Excellence:

  • Technologie-Radar: Du beobachtest technologische Entwicklungen, testest neue Lösungen und bewertest deren Nutzen für unser Unternehmen

  • Referenzimplementierungen: Du entwickelst wieder verwendbare KI-Bausteine, Blueprints und Best Practices für unsere Projektteams

  • Eigene Inferenz-Plattform weiterentwickeln: Du entwickelst unseren Modell-Stack und AI Gateway weiter, vergleichst Modelle und Inferenz-Technologien und schaffst Grundlagen für fundierte Technologieentscheidungen

  • Standards und Kostenkontrolle: Du definierst Standards für Prompt- und Agent-Engineering, Modellauswahl, Betriebskosten und Sicherheit und dokumentierst diese zentral

  • Befähigung in die Breite: Du vermittelst dein Wissen durch Schulungen, Demos und praxisnahe Leitlinien an unsere Mitarbeitenden

  • Vom Wissen zum Angebot: Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns aus neuen Erkenntnissen marktfähige KI-Angebote und Services


  • Abgeschlossenes Studium im IT- oder MINT-nahen Umfeld oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation

  • ≥ 5 Jahre Erfahrung als Software-, Data- oder ML-Engineer, davon mindestens 18 Monate mit produktiven LLM-basierten Systemen

  • Erfahrung mit mindestens einem produktiv eingesetzten agentischen System oder Workflow sowie mit RAG-Architekturen und der Bewertung ihrer Retrieval-Qualität

  • Deutschkenntnisse auf C1/C2 Niveau und Englischkenntnisse auf B2 Niveau

  • 20% Reisebereitschaft zu unseren Kunden bei Bedarf

  • Deutscher Wohnsitz

jobs.title: Stage Consumentengedrag
jobs.description:
Waarom pak je in de supermarkt het ene product wel uit het schap en het andere niet? Ligt het aan de verpakking? De prijs? Smaak? Gemak? Of simpelweg omdat het precies op de juiste plek staat?

Bij Growy telen we verse sla, kruiden en microgreens in Amsterdam in onze vertical farm. Vertical farming klinkt misschien ingewikkeld, maar het idee is simpel: we telen planten in lagen boven elkaar, midden in de stad en helemaal los van het weer buiten.
Nu onze producten in steeds meer Nederlandse supermarkten te vinden zijn, willen we onze consumenten nóg beter leren begrijpen. Daarom zoeken we een nieuwsgierige en commercieel ingestelde stagiair die zich wil verdiepen in consumentengedrag en inzichten kan vertalen naar echte commerciële kansen.

En nee, dit wordt geen stageproject wat ergens in een lade verdwijnt en niemand ooit nog bekijkt, jouw stage gaat voor ons echt een verschil maken!

🌱Wat ga je doen?

Hoe zorgen we ervoor dat meer consumenten Growy ontdekken, proberen én opnieuw kopen?

Tijdens je stage ga je bijvoorbeeld:

  • consumenten interviewen en/of focusgroepen organiseren;

  • onderzoeken wat mensen belangrijk vinden bij het kopen van verse salades en kruiden;

  • ontdekken welke drempels consumenten ervan weerhouden een product te proberen;

  • onderzoeken wat juist zorgt voor een herhaalaankoop;

  • kijken naar kansen rondom prijs, assortiment, verpakking, positionering, promoties en zichtbaarheid;

  • kwantitatief onderzoek, zoals enquêtes, opzetten om ideeën te testen;

  • jouw inzichten vertalen naar concrete commerciële en marketingaanbevelingen.

Aan het einde van je stage presenteer je jouw belangrijkste inzichten en aanbevelingen aan ons Sales & Marketing team. En als het binnen je stage past, kun je misschien zelfs één van je ideeën in de praktijk testen.

De precieze inhoud stemmen we af op de duur van je stage en de eisen vanuit jouw opleiding.

Goed om te weten; onze farm is nog volop in ontwikkeling, we zitten nog in onze start-up/scale-up fase. Dit betekent dat je naast je onderzoek ook tijd zult besteden aan andere zaken in onze farm. Dit geldt niet alleen voor jou als stagiair maar voor ons hele team. Zo draait iedereen uit kantoor maandelijks een shift in de farm, waarbij we helpen met zaaien, oogsten of verpakken.

🌱Wat kun je van ons verwachten?

  • Een unieke stageplek; wij bouwen aan de toekomst van voedselproductie;

  • Je wordt onderdeel van een klein team, er wordt naar je ideëen en input geluisterd;

  • We werken fulltime vanaf onze farm in Amsterdam;

  • Een maandelijkse stagevergoeding van 500 euro, we vergoeden geen andere zaken;

  • Veel ruimte en tijd voor creativiteit en een ‘ga het maar proberen!' mentaliteit

  • Een gezellige werksfeer waarin we graag samen na werk nog leuke dingen ondernemen


🌱Wat breng jij?

  • Je volgt een HBO of WO opleiding in Nederland en staat daar ingeschreven gedurende de hele stage periode. Qua studies denken wij in de richting marketing, bedrijfskunde of (commerciële) psychologie, maar wie weet volg jij een andere studie die ook goed aansluit 🙂

  • Fulltime beschikbaar voor 4 of 5 maanden, startdatum december 2026 of januari of februari 2027

  • Je hebt je rijbewijs B; je zult veel op pad zijn om supermarkten te bezoeken

  • Een flinke portie nieuwsgierigheid

  • Je bent sociaal; je stapt makkelijk op mensen af en maakt een praatje met ze

  • Je spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en kunt je ook goed redden in het Engels

  • Je bent een zelf-starter; we zullen je uiteraard begeleiden tijdens je stage, maar het initiatief voor de invulling en aanpak ligt bij jou

jobs.title: Senior Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Platform Engineer

Permanent employee · Full-time · Berlin (HQ)

 

Our Mission For You

European energy costs are twice as high as in the US and China, and electricity demand is expected to double by 2050. This puts European industry under massive cost pressure – and companies need to act now.

trawa is building the solution: the first integrated B2B energy platform that brings together energy procurement, energy management and the marketing of flexible assets in one product. This helps companies save up to 30% on their recurring electricity costs while switching to renewable energy.

We're the fastest-growing B2B energy platform in Europe. Active in Germany and Austria now, and expanding operations to a third market in 2027. We're on the road to European scale and move fast – the market window is open and we intend to own it.

Now we are looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to build the foundation every trawa engineer relies on.

 

About trawa

trawa is a tech-driven scale-up based in Berlin with around 100 employees, combining deep energy market expertise with in-house software development. We've raised over €35M to date, most recently a €24M Series A in May 2025, backed by Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic and Tiny VC. This role is based in our Berlin office, where we work together in person most of the week. We offer flexible working hours, so you can shape your day in a way that works for you.

 

The Team

Our Platform team owns our infrastructure, shared tooling and developer experience, so your work shapes how fast and how safely the whole company ships. You'll work with engineers across the company and see the impact of your work across every team.

 

Who We Are Looking For

  • Impact focus: You focus on impact, not just technical outcomes, and you care about what your work makes possible for others.

  • Natural collaborator: People enjoy working with you, and you build strong relationships across teams.

  • Platform experience: You have at least 8 years of experience in a platform, DevOps or SRE role.

  • Hands-on AWS and IaC: You have deep hands-on experience with AWS and infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform.

  • Distributed systems: You have built or run distributed services in production, with a strong grasp of security, reliability, observability and cost efficiency.

 

What You'll Do

  • Build and run scalable, secure, highly available AWS infrastructure that powers our mission-critical services.

  • Improve CI/CD pipelines, observability tooling and internal platforms so teams ship faster and with confidence.

  • Embed security into our infrastructure and pipelines, covering access management, secrets and compliance needs.

  • Partner with engineers, share best practices and make the right way the easy way.

 

Our Tech Stack

  • AWS, Terraform, Spacelift, Docker, GitHub Actions

  • Python, TypeScript

  • Dash0, Sentry, Incident.io

 

90 Day Goals

After 6 Weeks (Onboarding):

  • Current setup: You have a comprehensive understanding of trawa's current tech stack, infrastructure and security posture.

  • Team relationships: You have met the engineering teams, learned how they build, ship and run their services, and developed relationships with your key stakeholders.

Month 3 (Ramp-Up):

  • Infrastructure ownership: You own parts of our AWS infrastructure and Terraform codebase.

  • Workflow friction: You have found the biggest friction points in our developer workflow and proposed ways to fix them.

  • Platform improvement: You have led a meaningful platform improvement from design to rollout.

 

Why Us?

Impact: European SMEs spend between €150k and €10M per year on electricity – most are overpaying and locked into outdated procurement. Your work will directly change how thousands of companies buy, manage and use energy. The impact is measurable, the market is massive, and the timing is now.

Ownership: We empower our team members to take ownership of their work and drive results, regardless of background or experience level.

Learning & Growth: We provide an annual budget and dedicated time for professional development. You'll have opportunities for mentorship, learning and career progression.

Diversity and Inclusion: We're an equal opportunity employer, and our team reflects that. Our organisation brings together over 15 nationalities, contributing a variety of languages, experiences and perspectives. At trawa, we're family-friendly with parents across all levels, and our diversity is represented throughout the company, including leadership. We're committed to an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

Package & Benefits: We offer a competitive compensation package including salary and stock options, 30 days of vacation, and a range of benefits including subsidies for home internet and lunches, a Sports Club membership, dedicated learning days with an annual learning budget, plus a weekly team lunch and regular team events.

At trawa, we're dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly, we encourage you to apply – you may be the right fit for this or another opportunity.

You will work closely with global colleagues to provide practical, business-oriented advice that enables growth while managing risk across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Proactive, business-minded, and committed to delivering practical solutions that support both compliance and commercial success.

What you bring

  • Law degree and qualification to practice law in Germany.

  • 7+ years of relevant post-qualification legal experience (in-house experience in technology or SaaS strongly preferred).

Shape the service around static and agentic workflows, with support for additional analysis types guided by validated customer needs.

The domain covers issue-processing pipelines, durable storage, and supporting APIs and events. You will agree the scope and ownership of shared execution orchestration and other expanded capabilities with engine, infrastructure, and consuming-product teams. Engine teams retain detection logic; consuming teams retain their product workflows and acceptance criteria; workflow and Quality Gate owners retain publication, policy, and merge decisions.

Your direct customers are the technical teams building analysis engines, agent services, guidance capabilities, and other products on this service. Success is the value these teams deliver to developers and enterprises, not the number of shared capabilities shipped.

Agree contracts for issue identity and state changes with engine and workflow owners, keeping processing separate from publication and policy decisions.

Senior Mechanical Design Engineer (Power Electronics)
jobs.description:
Hyperscale Power is building the power backbone for the AI data center era: a complete power conversion chain from 13.8kV–35kV medium-voltage AC down to 800V DC, combining ultra-compact SiC-based power blocks. Our Solid-State Transformers (SSTs) are the core of this revolution, providing unprecedented control, efficiency, and compactness.

As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer, you will turn our power electronic modules into a robust, compact and safe product. You will design how the SiC-based power modules, magnetics, busbars and cooling come together into one unit, working closely with our power electronics, magnetics and thermal engineers.

Instead of handing your designs over for someone else to build, you take them all the way: you calculate them, build and assemble the prototypes yourself in our workshop, and take the design from first prototype to a product ready for series production.

This role is for you if…

you've designed the mechanical integration of power electronics or other electronic systems and know your way around creepage, clearance and insulating plastics. You back your designs with solid calculations, and you're as comfortable with a screwdriver in the workshop as with CAD at your desk.

This role isn't for you if…

your experience is in classic mechanical design only, such as gears, gearboxes or pumps, or you prefer to stay at your desk while someone else builds your prototypes. It's also not a fit if you need technicians for assembly or established processes before you can start.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design the mechanical integration of power electronic modules into the SST: enclosures, holders, fixtures and jigs, and interfaces to the busbar system, with a modular design approach.

  • Model and design electro-mechanical parts and assemblies, including plastics, sheet metal, insulation systems, magnetic components and cooling system interfaces.

  • Ensure electrical safety through the design on both the medium-voltage and low-voltage side: creepage and clearance distances, CTI and material selection, electrical isolation and sealing.

  • Design for manufacturing, assembly and test from the first concept, working with suppliers on processes such as injection molding, sheet metal and machining.

  • Own the DFMEA for your designs and drive the resulting actions into the design.

  • Validate designs with structural FEA, including static, modal, shock and vibration analysis, before they are released for production, and correlate the results with test data.

  • Build and assemble prototypes and test assemblies hands-on in our workshop, together with the engineering team, using additive manufacturing where it speeds things up.

  • Collaborate with other engineers to take designs from concept through prototype to series production.

  • Share your expertise and support other engineers on best practices in mechanical engineering.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.

  • 4+ years of full-time industry experience in mechanical design, with a focus on the mechanical integration of power electronics or other electronic systems.

  • Proven experience applying DFM and DFA to your own designs, with parts and assemblies that made it into production.

  • Hands-on experience leading or actively contributing to DFMEAs.

  • Strong experience with structural FEA (e.g. ANSYS), including static, modal, shock and vibration analysis. You set up the models yourself and use the results to drive design decisions.

  • Solid knowledge of creepage, clearance, CTI, insulation coordination and electrical safety (e.g. IEC 60664-1, IEC 62477-1), ideally up to medium voltage.

  • Solid experience designing with polymers/plastics, ideally for electronics integration.

  • Proficiency in 3D CAD (e.g. SolidWorks), GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis.

  • Hands-on experience building and assembling prototypes in a professional setting.

  • Experience with environmental, reliability and safety standards for power delivery products.

  • Basic understanding of electrical design fundamentals; familiarity with PCBAs and PCBA components.

  • Strong organization, written and verbal communication skills.

  • Fluent English; German is a plus.

  • Eligible to work in Switzerland (Swiss or EU/EFTA citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit).

The job will be located at our HQ in Egg b. Zürich, Switzerland.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with industrialization: taking hardware from prototype to series production and designing with series production in mind from the start (tooling such as injection molds, supplier involvement, cost and process capability).

  • Experience with high-volume manufacturing and automated assembly processes.

  • Experience with additive manufacturing (e.g. SLA, SLS, FDM) for prototypes, fixtures and jigs, ideally including insulating or flame-retardant materials.

  • Experience with PFMEA, DFT and DFR.

  • Experience with insulation design for medium voltage, including partial discharge.

  • Experience with liquid cooling integration or CFD.

Benefits

  • Equity + competitive salary.

  • Unique technology and market opportunity – design the hardware of a new product category for the energy transition.

  • Hybrid work with flexible working times.

Rivia is a technology company building a data engine that powers the future of clinical trial intelligence. Rivia was founded on the belief that new drugs can be brought to market more successfully with a fraction of today's capital.

Biotechs are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is constantly constrained by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia unifies clinical trial data at scale through a core engine built as a reusable intelligence layer, comprising hundreds of configurations and trial-specific logic, independent of source structure. This vertical stack of data engine, workflows, and agents creates a distinct advantage in how trials are operated.

Over the past two years, European and US based biotechs running global clinical trials on Rivia have demonstrated measurable impact, from earlier understanding of therapeutic potential to significantly more efficient trial execution. In March 2026, Rivia raised its $15M Series A led by Earlybird Venture Capital.

WHO WE ARE 🌍

Want to own how the backend works for everyone, not just one corner of it?

We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer who works across PHP and Python and wants a say in the bigger picture. You’ll lead company-level projects like our Auth Service: one authorization layer for PHP and Python, so Python products can handle their traffic directly instead of going through PHP. When things are unclear, you’ll research first, weigh the trade-offs and write them down. Then you’ll ship in small, safe steps. You’ll also decide where code should live based on what’s best for the system, not on which language you know best.

YOUR FUTURE TEAMMATES 👋

Meet the Backend Platform team:

We're a small team of engineers from core PHP, Infra, and AI backgrounds. We lead technical initiatives across the whole backend and own its health. Product teams build and run their own components, and we give them the tools, standards, and expertise to do it well. Each of us leads our own project, from planning to agreeing with other teams to production. We work in weekly cycles and write our decisions down. Right now we're bringing PHP and Python platform work together into one common backend platform.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 🚀

  • Lead company-level technical projects end to end, from design and planning to rollout and support, such as completing our Auth Service development and shaping authorization as a separate layer for PHP and Python.

AIM Solutions is an early-stage deep-tech startup in Eindhoven building inspection and metrology equipment for the semiconductor industry. We are in an active build phase, small, and growing.

The role
You own how our tool is controlled and operated. The machine combines lasers, high-speed cameras, a nanometer-precision wafer stage and GPU-based image reconstruction. Every measurement depends on these parts working together in tight synchronization. You are the system engineer for that layer: the control architecture, the timing, the machine software, and the data path from sensor to result. You work side by side with our system engineer for the metrology hardware and with our algorithms team, and together you lead the system.

You will:

  • Own the system control architecture: machine software, control hardware, timing and synchronization, and the data path from acquisition to reconstruction

  • Translate system performance and throughput goals into requirements for control, software and compute, and keep them traceable

  • Own the timing, throughput and data budgets, and decide where time is won or lost in a measurement

  • Define and guard the interfaces between control software, hardware and algorithms, including the hardware abstraction layer

  • Define how the machine is operated: machine states, sequencing, recipes, error handling, logging and monitoring

  • Steer the software and embedded engineers on the control side: set priorities, run design reviews and resolve trade-offs

  • Set up integration and verification of the control layer, with a test strategy that keeps it reliable as the hardware changes between builds

  • Carry the machine software from lab prototype toward a production tool that runs unattended in a fab

Your profile

jobs.title: Mobile Developer
jobs.description:
At Luscii, we develop several applications within the OMRON Digital Health Circle, including the Luscii Thuismeten app and OMRON Connect. Together, we build technology that makes healthcare more accessible, giving patients and healthcare professionals more space to focus on care. As a Mobile Developer, you will contribute to this mission by developing and improving the applications that connect people, devices and healthcare.

Our digital health solutions enable healthcare professionals to monitor patients remotely, helping people receive the right care in the right place. You will work across our mobile applications, creating reliable, intuitive and high-performing experiences for patients and healthcare professionals alike.

Beyond developing and improving our apps, you will help shape our technical direction, explore new technologies and share your expertise with colleagues. You will have the autonomy to take ownership, make technical decisions and contribute beyond your immediate responsibilities, supported by Luscii's Holacratic way of working.

Your role

As a Mobile Developer at Luscii, you will take ownership of the development, optimisation and maintenance of our mobile applications across iOS and Android. You bring ideas to life, make well-considered technical decisions and help ensure our applications remain performant, stable, scalable and easy to maintain.

You will work closely with colleagues across development, QA and support, combining hands-on engineering with technical ownership. Whether you are building a new feature, exploring a technology through a proof of concept or resolving a production issue, you will help us continuously improve the quality and usability of our digital health solutions.

What you will be doing:

  • Develop, maintain and optimise mobile applications using native technologies such as Kotlin and Swift, with a focus on performance, stability and user experience.

  • Contribute to mobile architecture, technical design and modular codebases, applying clean architecture, object-oriented design principles and patterns such as MVVM and MVI.

  • Build intuitive user interfaces using technologies such as Jetpack Compose and SwiftUI, following platform-specific design guidelines.

  • Develop and maintain features that communicate with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices, as well as web services, cloud platforms and APIs.

  • Build prototypes and proof of concepts to explore new technologies, validate technical approaches and identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Investigate and resolve production issues through debugging and performance analysis, covering areas such as memory management, multithreading and networking.

  • Contribute to code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD processes, sharing technical knowledge and helping colleagues make sound implementation decisions.

Why Luscii?

Read more about working at Luscii and how we work at Luscii/OMRON. Together, we are working on a mission to create space for care. Freedom, autonomy and ownership are of great importance in this. You are responsible for your own results and work according to the principles of Holacracy.

Most important benefits

  • Salary: € 4.600 - € 5.900 gross per month (based on 32 hours per week – that’s full-time at Luscii).

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in The Netherlands. We stay connected through monthly in-person team days called Assemblii.

  • Flexible setup: Create your own ideal workspace. Whatever works best for you - we’ve got you covered here.

The ideal candidate…

… probably doesn't exist, but if you can tick most of the checkboxes below, please apply! We are looking for somebody who is comfortable in taking ownership and making well-considered decisions independently. You enjoy the autonomy to shape your work and responsibilities, while actively seeking collaboration and alignment with others.

You know when to step up, when to involve colleagues and when to move forward decisively. Working independently does not mean working in isolation for you. You feel at ease being both a self-starter and a committed team player, contributing to shared goals while taking responsibility for your own domain. You value open communication, transparency, and mutual trust.

  • You have at least five years of experience in mobile development, with a strong background in native Android and/or iOS development. You have extensive experience with Kotlin and/or Swift.

  • You have a relevant bachelor's degree, for example in Computer Science or Computer Engineering and you are familiar with working in an Agile environment.

  • You have a solid understanding of mobile architecture and software design principles, including clean architecture, object-oriented design, MVVM and/or MVI. You know how to build and maintain modular applications.

  • You have experience with mobile development frameworks and tools such as Jetpack Compose, SwiftUI, Kotlin Coroutines, Flow and Kotlin Multiplatform. You are also familiar with unit testing and/or UI testing, CI/CD pipelines and platform-specific design guidelines.

  • You understand what it takes to build reliable, high-performing mobile applications, including memory management, multithreading, networking, debugging and optimisation. You have experience integrating web services, cloud technologies, APIs and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices.

  • You are open to working in a Holacratic organization and curious about our way of organizing work, roles, and responsibilities;

  • English is our primary language for all internal communication at Luscii, so you're fluent in that language.

Interested? Apply now!

Would you like more information? Feel free to contact our recruiter Björn Bogerd via

We organise three interviews for each vacancy. It is an extensive process, but we want to ensure that there is a good fit in regards to a potential collaboration, our culture and our way of working. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Partner Integrations
jobs.description:
About the team

Most providers make customers migrate their data to them. We're doing the opposite: bringing ClickHouse Cloud into the environments our customers already trust, so their data stays useful right where it lives.

Those environments come in a few shapes. Some are major cloud data platforms that run ClickHouse as a native service, so customers get it without leaving the tool they already use. Some are BI and visualization tools that need ClickHouse to show up as a fast, first-class data source behind their dashboards. And some are developer and data platforms we connect through marketplaces and identity federation with a couple of clicks or agentic calls. Every integration is unique, but the goal is the same every time: ClickHouse should feel like a first-class citizen in every environment.

The craft is finding the patterns underneath different integrations. As one of the first backend engineers, you'll help shape the technical defaults for this team. You'll have end-to-end ownership, but you'll also work inside the constraints of platforms you don't own: thin documentation, unfamiliar deployment topologies, and timelines governed by partner approval cycles. A lot of the challenge is engineering across trust boundaries you don't fully control.

You won't be doing it alone. You'll work closely with your engineering manager, the product manager, a growing team, and experienced engineers across the broader org. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, let's talk.

What you'll do

You'll own an integration end to end: the design, the code, and the production system that keeps running after launch. The patterns you set there become defaults the rest of the team builds on.

Day to day, that looks like:

  • Owning the architecture: auth and identity flows, multi-tenancy, how data moves and where it's allowed to live, performance, and what happens in production

  • Running what you build. Which means owning the infrastructure, CI, deployment, observability behind it and on-call

  • Working on top of external platforms you can't change, and being straight about which risks are yours to manage and which aren't

  • Partnering closely with the internal teams whose services you depend on: iterating on product requirements, agreeing on interfaces and protocols, and proactively finding ways to keep moving

About you

These are the attributes of someone who will perform well in this role:

  • 8+ years building software, with a good chunk of it on data-heavy or integration-flavored systems

  • Preferably proficient in TypeScript or Go or comfortable contributing to each

  • Solid backend and systems instincts. You can reason about deployment topology, multi-tenancy, and data movement, and you're comfortable owning architectural tradeoffs you'll have to live with later

  • You've worked with modern auth protocols, service principals, and identity federation, and you know how to get it right across a trust boundary

  • You've built on someone else's platform and know what that's actually like: incomplete docs, unintended breaking changes, etc.

  • You're comfortable in ambiguity. You can ship before the spec is finished, make sensible calls under uncertainty, and flag the decisions that'll be hard to undo to your team before we bake them in.

  • You're good with other engineers. Much of the work runs through teams you don't own, and you earn their trust by how you think, not just what you commit.

  • You're mainly a backend engineer, but you're comfortable enough to touch a modern React app

  • You use AI tools well and honestly. Reach for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or whatever helps, and be clear about where you did and didn't

  • You write well. Most of how we coordinate happens async in chats, design docs and RFCs

Nice to have

None of these are required, but any of them would be a bonus:

  • Close familiarity with a major cloud data or analytics platform ecosystem

  • Real depth in auth and identity federation, or experience building to a partner's security review, marketplace requirements or certification requirements

  • Hands-on experience designing multi-tenant SaaS platforms, or the isolation and deployment topology behind them

  • Working knowledge of ClickHouse, or another columnar / OLAP engine

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

jobs.title: New Business Manager
jobs.description:
Our company

Surfer is an AI Visibility Platform that helps marketing teams become the definitive answer wherever their buyers search — across Google and AI search. The platform combines data, research-backed optimization, and a user-friendly workflow to grow brand visibility through content where buying decisions start to form.

Surfer is used by content marketers, SEO specialists, agencies, and in-house marketing teams around the world to track, plan, write, and optimize content that gets ranked and cited by both search engines and LLMs.

Surfer is part of Positive Group - a fast-growing tech group specializing in B2B SaaS products that help marketing teams grow smarter. The group brings together several brands around a common ambition: to become the European benchmark in MarTech. With around 400 employees based in France, Germany, Italy, and Poland, Positive supports customers in 80+ countries.

We’re a remote-first company, but if you ever crave some in-person energy, we’ve got a cozy office in Wrocław , Poland where the magic happens (and coffee never runs out ☕).


About the role

We're looking for someone who's worked at a marketing/SEO agency or a martech company and knows what it takes to close - someone who picks up the phone without thinking twice, and who hasn't been trained out of that instinct by years of "process."

On a day-to-day basis, you'll own the new-business side end-to-end: prospecting and building your own pipeline, working the leads that come your way, qualifying them, running discovery and demos, negotiating, and closing. You'll work closely with the Customer Success team, and get support from Marketing and RevOps. This role rewards initiative - the more you build and close, the more it shows, both in your results and in what you earn.

You will be responsible for:

  • Work both sides of the pipeline: reaching out to existing leads in our CRM (conference, meetup, webinar, and community signals plus records of past interest) while building a new pipeline from scratch through your own outbound prospecting.

  • Prospect actively: research target accounts, identify decision-makers, and open conversations with agencies and in-house teams that haven’t reached out to us yet.

  • Run multi-channel outreach on these leads across email, LinkedIn, and phone.

  • Build and continuously refine ICP-aligned contact lists covering both marketing/SEO agencies and in-house SEO/marketing teams at companies.

  • Qualify leads and run discovery calls, demos, and negotiations, owning the deal through to signed contract and payment.

Requirements:

  • Minimum 4 years of B2B sales experience as an SDR/BDR/AE at a marketing/SEO agency, a martech company (e.g. SEO, content, analytics, or marketing automation software), or at a company selling into agencies.

  • Proven track record of closing deals end-to-end, including negotiation and contracting.

  • Familiarity with the SEO/content marketing space (content briefs, topical authority, SERPs).

  • No hesitation picking up the phone the moment a lead is worth chasing.

  • Motivated by closing deals, not just running a process. You know the satisfaction of seeing a deal through from first call to signed contract - and you want more of that.

  • Outreach experience across email, LinkedIn, and phone.

  • Familiarity with CRM and sales/outbound tools.

  • Strong written and verbal English (C1 or above).

  • Nice to have: experience selling a SaaS product (not a service); ABM (account-based marketing/sales) experience.

What we offer:

We build the team around experts and stay out of their way. That starts with the basics:

Compensation: $36,000–45,500/year base (excl. VAT, where applicable), plus a bonus system.

Contract: We work exclusively on B2B (contractor) agreements. This means you’ll need your own registered business (e.g. sole proprietorship / self-employed status in your country) and will invoice us monthly.

We take care of the things that matter outside the work itself - your health, your rest, the setup that lets you work well, and the chance to sharpen your craft. Everything else follows from how we operate: trust over control, outcomes over hours.

Location and Remote Work:

We’re a remote-first company, but if you ever crave some in-person energy, we’ve got a cozy office in Wrocław, Poland.
